greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who calls us to be faithful stewards of his love, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to serve with a humble heart. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the source of all grace and strength. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you promise that the labor of the just is never in vain. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The salvation of the just comes from the Lord.
homily:
We begin today with a simple, quiet image: the apron. Think of it. It is not a garment of status or power. It is a garment of work. It is the piece of fabric tied around the waist of the one who is busy serving, the one who is moving between the stove and the table, the one who is focused entirely on the needs of others. In the Gospel today, Jesus speaks of the servant who comes in from the field, tired from plowing or tending sheep, and is told to put on his apron and wait at the table. It sounds, at first, like a hard word. We live in a world that wants to be thanked, to be recognized, to be told that we have done enough. We want to be able to hang up our tools and be served. But Jesus invites us into a different rhythm—a rhythm of quiet, steady faithfulness that does not look for applause, but finds its joy in simply doing what is asked of us.

I want you to hold onto this image: the apron. It is the image of a life that is poured out, not because it is forced, but because it is rooted in love. It is the image of the grace that Benjamin Vo carried—a grace that was not about the accolades of the world, but about the quiet, consistent way he showed up for his family and his friends. It is the image of a heart that understands that our true worth is not found in the ledger of our accomplishments, but in the simple, holy act of belonging to God.

Let us speak the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been four months since he moved from this life into the fullness of God’s presence. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the brilliant, curious mind that loved to explore the architecture of the world, the gentle, respectful spirit that made him such a treasure—are suddenly interrupted by the sharp, cold realization that he is not there in the way he once was. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary Tuesday. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. 

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Listen to what Jesus says: 'When you have done all you have been commanded, say, We are unprofitable servants; we have done what we were obliged to do.' It sounds like a call to humility, and it is. But it is also a call to freedom. When we stop trying to prove our worth, when we stop trying to earn our place at the table, we are free to simply receive the love that is already there. Benjamin understood this. Think of the way he moved through the world—not with a sense of entitlement, but with a sense of wonder. Think of his brilliant mind, the way he coded those games on GitHub, or how he would talk about his ‘con chim airlines’ with such a genuine, infectious giggle. He wasn't trying to build an empire; he was trying to build a connection. He was trying to share a joy. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who is now at the banquet of heaven, interceding for you. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God. He has found the destination he was searching for, and he is waiting for the rest of his family to arrive.

Consider the first reading from Titus: 'For the grace of God has appeared, saving all and training us to reject godless ways and worldly desires and to live temperately, justly, and devoutly in this age.' This is the training of the heart. It is the discipline of love. Benjamin’s life was a testament to this grace. Think of that remarkable moment when he unprompted told his parents that he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love. That love is still flowing. It flows in the well dedicated in his name, it flows in the meals shared in his honor, and it flows in the kindness you show to one another every single day. He was a servant of love, and he is still serving you from the other side.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming.

We hear in the Psalm: 'Trust in the LORD and do good, that you may dwell in the land and be fed in security. Take delight in the LORD, and he will grant you your heart’s requests.' This is the turn of the heart. The salvation of the just is not a reward for our labor; it is a gift of God’s presence. We do not work to earn heaven; we work because we are already loved. We serve because we have already been served by the One who washed our feet. Benjamin is now resting in that security. He is dwelling in the land of the living, and he is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected in the sight of God.

Think of the dream you had, Alan. You were waiting in line to buy ice cream, and Ben paid. That is the image of the kingdom. It is the image of the one who has gone before us, the one who is now in the position of the steward of grace, waiting to welcome you. He is not distant. He is not gone. He is simply ahead, preparing the way. He is the one who will one day stand at the door of the Father’s house and say, 'I am here, and my family is with me.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was a reminder that the bond you share is not broken by death. It is only changed, deepened, and held in the eternal keeping of God. He is well, he is strong, and he is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected in the sight of God.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is the one who has already passed the test, as he said in your dream: 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết.' He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, cheeky grin, looking out toward an endless horizon. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity, holding the key. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of his face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our dear Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ and find their home at the banquet of heaven.
For all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that God may console them, strengthen their hearts, and fill them with the hope of a joyful reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Beloved:
You must say what is consistent with sound doctrine,
namely, that older men should be temperate, dignified,
self-controlled, sound in faith, love, and endurance.
Similarly, older women should be reverent in their behavior,
not slanderers, not addicted to drink,
teaching what is good, so that they may train younger women
to love their husbands and children,
to be self-controlled, chaste, good homemakers,
under the control of their husbands,
so that the word of God may not be discredited.Urge the younger men, similarly, to control themselves,
showing yourself as a model of good deeds in every respect,
with integrity in your teaching, dignity, and sound speech
that cannot be criticized,
so that the opponent will be put to shame
without anything bad to say about us.For the grace of God has appeared, saving all
and training us to reject godless ways and worldly desires
and to live temperately, justly, and devoutly in this age,
as we await the blessed hope,
the appearance of the glory of the great God
and of our savior Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for us to deliver us from all lawlessness
and to cleanse for himself a people as his own,
eager to do what is good.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R.    (39a) The salvation of the just comes from the Lord.
Trust in the LORD and do good,
that you may dwell in the land and be fed in security.
Take delight in the LORD,
and he will grant you your heart’s requests.
R.    The salvation of the just comes from the Lord.
The LORD watches over the lives of the wholehearted;
their inheritance lasts forever.
By the LORD are the steps of a man made firm,
and he approves his way.
R.    The salvation of the just comes from the Lord.
Turn from evil and do good,
that you may abide forever;
The just shall possess the land
and dwell in it forever.
R.    The salvation of the just comes from the Lord.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to the Apostles:
“Who among you would say to your servant
who has just come in from plowing or tending sheep in the field,
‘Come here immediately and take your place at table’?
Would he not rather say to him,
‘Prepare something for me to eat.
Put on your apron and wait on me while I eat and drink.
You may eat and drink when I am finished’?
Is he grateful to that servant because he did what was commanded?
So should it be with you.
When you have done all you have been commanded, say,
‘We are unprofitable servants;
we have done what we were obliged to do.’”

pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
